decisions.rationale: The artifact exists, its canonicalUrl matches the cited URL, the offsets exactly slice the retained extract, and the extract literally states that Purple Haze was originally written backstage at Billy Walker's Upper Cut Club on December 26, 1966.

The artifact exists, its canonicalUrl matches the cited URL, the offsets exactly slice the retained extract, and the extract states that after scrapping March rough mixes Chandler returned with Kramer and Hendrix to mix the final released version of Manic Depression.

The artifact exists, its canonicalUrl matches the cited URL, the offsets exactly slice the retained extract, and the extract reports Noel Redding's recollection that Chandler had the Experience record nearly 30 takes of Hey Joe for the final mix.

The artifact exists, its canonicalUrl matches the cited URL, the offsets exactly slice the retained extract, and Kramer's quoted statement describes linking panning to Hendrix's rhythm guitar and timing it to the bending guitar note on Love or Confusion.

The artifact exists, its canonicalUrl matches the cited URL, the offsets exactly slice the retained extract, and the extract states that May This Be Love had the working title Waterfall and used a backward-sounding guitar effect that Hendrix played forward.

The artifact exists, its canonicalUrl matches the cited URL, the offsets exactly slice the retained extract, and the extract states that Hendrix used an early hand-operated wah-wah effects unit on I Don't Live Today before the foot-pedal model replaced it.

The artifact exists, its canonicalUrl matches the cited URL, the offsets exactly slice the retained extract, and Chandler's quoted recollection says The Wind Cries Mary was recorded at the tail end of the Fire session without rehearsal and that the whole thing was done in 20 minutes.

The artifact exists, its canonicalUrl matches the cited URL, the offsets exactly slice the retained extract, and the extract states that Fire's basic track was recorded after seven takes while Hendrix experimented with tempo during early takes.

The artifact exists, its canonicalUrl matches the cited URL, the offsets exactly slice the retained extract, and Chandler's quoted recollection says Hendrix read his science-fiction books and that Third Stone From the Sun and Up From the Skies came from that reading.

The artifact exists, its canonicalUrl matches the cited URL, the offsets exactly slice the retained extract, and the extract states that a rough mix of Foxey Lady was recorded at CBS Studios while Mitch Mitchell was absent.

The artifact exists, its canonicalUrl matches the cited URL, the offsets exactly slice the retained extract, and the extract states that Are You Experienced? used a fourth track for backward guitar, bass, and percussion, recorded forward and then reversed through a second machine.

The artifact exists, its canonicalUrl matches the cited URL, the offsets exactly slice the retained extract, and the extract states Chandler needed a B-side for Hey Joe, pressured Hendrix to write a new song, and that Stone Free was the first Experience song Hendrix wrote.

The artifact exists, its canonicalUrl matches the cited URL, the offsets exactly slice the retained extract, and the extract states that 51st Anniversary was the first Experience composition to use overdubbing as a production strategy, with Chandler recalling five linked guitar overdubs.

The artifact exists, its canonicalUrl matches the cited URL, the offsets exactly slice the retained extract, and the extract states that Highway Chile was chosen as the B-side to The Wind Cries Mary and omitted from the full album release.

The artifact exists, its canonicalUrl matches the cited URL, the offsets exactly slice the retained extract, and the extract states that Hendrix developed rhythm patterns for Can You See Me with his Stratocaster and a small Vox amplifier.

The artifact exists, its canonicalUrl matches the cited URL, the offsets exactly slice the retained extract, and Chandler's quoted statement says Remember began as an end-of-session DeLane Lea demo and that little of the original remained after Hendrix tightened it at Olympic.

The artifact exists, its canonicalUrl matches the cited URL, the offsets exactly slice the retained extract, and Chandler's quoted recollection says Noel played rhythm guitar as the bass line on Red House before it was remixed and added to the album.
